name: subselect_membership
comment: SubSelect eager loading: the target filters by membership in the root query, projected to the correlating property. The subquery renders through the same renderer, binds inline (@c0, @c1 continue the outer order), and keeps its paging; the outer select is unaliased on every dialect because the membership is single-property.

sqlite.sql: select id, user_id, status, amount, version, note, created_at, updated_at from transactions where user_id in (select id from users where name = @c0 order by name limit @c1) order by id

sqlserver.sql: select [id], [user_id], [status], [amount], [version], [note], [created_at], [updated_at] from [transactions] where [user_id] in (select [id] from [users] where [name] = @c0 order by [name] offset 0 rows fetch next @c1 rows only) order by [id]

postgres.sql: select "id", "user_id", "status", "amount", "version", "note", "created_at", "updated_at" from "transactions" where "user_id" in (select "id" from "users" where "name" = @c0 order by "name" limit @c1) order by "id"
